description: Direct fetch of the EKR public procedure listing (https://ekr.gov.hu/portal/kozbeszerzes/eljarasok/) returned a Hungarian maintenance notice rather than content.

result.result_summary: Maintenance page 'Sajnáljuk, a rendszeren karbantartást végzünk' with a pointer to ujvilag.gov.hu planned-refresh schedule. Recorded as unverified, NOT as dead — EKR is a legally mandatory live system.

why_it_matters: The primary cell source could not be inspected directly in this pass, so its exact search-URL patterns, CPV filter parameters and pagination behaviour remain unmapped; the collector design must be validated against the live system.

description: No documented public API or bulk-download endpoint was found for the Közbeszerzési Értesítő / kozbeszerzes.hu notice database.

result.result_summary: The Értesítő landing page exposes only HTML search, saved-search alerting and per-issue signed PDFs (pattern https://www.kozbeszerzes.hu/media/issue/pdf/signed/KE-YYYY-NN_.pdf). No API documentation surfaced in hu or en searches.

why_it_matters: National-only (below-EU-threshold) banking/payments notices — likely the majority of municipal account-management and POS contracts — must be obtained by HTML/PDF harvesting or via TED-derived third-party datasets, raising fragility and parsing cost.

description: No individual Hungarian banking/payments tender or award notice (e.g. a specific bankszámla-vezetés or kártyaelfogadás contract) was retrieved and confirmed in this pass.

result.result_summary: Local-language searches for 'számlavezetési szolgáltatás közbeszerzés eredménytájékoztató' returned only the Értesítő issue PDFs generically, not a resolvable individual notice.

why_it_matters: Confirms the finding that HU notice content is locked inside daily PDFs and JS search UIs rather than being individually indexed by web search — the collection pipeline cannot rely on search engines and must query the registers directly.

description: Red Flags (redflags.eu) risk-monitoring tool for Hungarian procurement is reported as not updated since 27 October 2023.

result.result_summary: Cause given is a change of the TED data source; the site remains up as a historical corpus.

why_it_matters: Ruling it out as a live signal prevents building a monitoring dependency on a dead feed; its historical corpus and red-flag methodology remain reusable.

description: The main Hungarian tender-monitoring vendors (tender-ertesito.hu, khf.hu, kozbeszerzesmonitor.hu, napitender.hu, innotender.hu) are subscription-gated.

result.result_summary: All advertise paid subscriptions (some with trials); none disclosed an open API or data-export terms permitting redistribution.

why_it_matters: These cannot be scraped and must be treated as licensed cross-checks; budgeting or a licensing decision is needed if completeness assurance is required.

description: The CoRe contract register public search was cited only as http://kereso.core.kt.hu, and the legacy KBA database uses Oracle APEX session-id URLs.

result.result_summary: Neither endpoint was inspected in this pass; deep links may be unstable or migrated.

why_it_matters: Contract-level values and pre-2018 history are the two layers most likely to break silently in a collector; they need explicit endpoint verification before being scheduled.

description: Searched for a standalone Hungarian RRF procurement portal at rrf.gov.hu; no such dedicated portal surfaced. RRF content appears to live under palyazat.gov.hu and sectoral institution sites (e.g. okfo.gov.hu, ikk.hu).

result.result_summary: No evidence of a separate rrf.gov.hu procurement site; treat palyazat.gov.hu as the RRF hub.

why_it_matters: Avoids wasted crawler configuration against a non-existent domain and concentrates monitoring on the real hub.

description: Local-language searching for procurement procedures used to select financial intermediaries for EU-funded financial instruments (közvetítő kiválasztás közbeszerzés) returned programme marketing pages only, not procedure documentation.

result.result_summary: Intermediary-selection procedure documents for GINOP Plusz financial instruments were not located in this pass.

why_it_matters: This is the mechanism by which commercial banks gain access to EU-funded lending volume; if it is not published as a classic tender, a different collection route (MFB corporate disclosures, ministry decrees) is required.

description: TED XML bulk-package URL patterns (/packages/daily/{OJS}, /packages/monthly/{yyyy-n}) were reported in secondary summaries of TED documentation rather than confirmed on the live TED page during this pass.

result.result_summary: Pattern recorded as a hypothesis to be confirmed against the TED developers' corner before automation.

why_it_matters: Building a backfill pipeline on an unconfirmed URL pattern risks silent collection failure.

description: Direct search for an actual Hungarian TED notice under CPV 66110000 returned only generic TED explainer pages and one German (D-Aalen) banking-services record; no HU notice was retrieved through general web search.

result.result_summary: General web search is not a viable discovery channel for individual HU banking notices; the TED search interface/API must be queried directly.

why_it_matters: Confirms that the collection method for this cell must be API-first, not search-engine-first.

description: The Közbeszerzési Hatóság 'Döntőbizottsági és bírósági határozatok' search page was fetched and its ~20 filter fields inventoried, but the page documents no API, no bulk export and no stated download format for decisions.

result.result_summary: Rich filtering (including CPV) but retrieval appears to be one-record-at-a-time through a web form; a save-search feature exists which hints at parameterised URLs worth reverse-engineering.

why_it_matters: Collection design for the highest-value source in this cell will need form-driven harvesting rather than a feed, raising cost and fragility.

description: Hungarian-language searches combining KDB remedies terms with banking terms (bankszámla-vezetés, jogorvoslat) returned only the institutional/portal layer, not individual banking-sector decisions.

result.result_summary: General web search does not surface individual D.xxx/yyyy decisions on banking or payment-service tenders; those appear to be reachable only through the on-site database, not through general indexing.

why_it_matters: Means the cell cannot be covered by search-engine monitoring alone — the KDB/KH databases must be queried directly with CPV 66xxxxxx and banking keywords.

description: No public repository of individual EUTAF audit reports or irregularity (szabálytalansági) decisions was found; only summary presentations, internal instructions and an ÁSZ audit of EUTAF itself.

result.result_summary: EUTAF publishes institutional material, not case-level audit findings.

why_it_matters: Audit-level detail on EU-funded procurement (including any banking/IT payments contracts) is largely non-public and would need FOI requests.

description: The EPPO/OLAF Hungarian-language search returned several content-farm domains (frisshir24, nagyireceptje, napjainkportal) republishing sensational claims about EPPO in Hungary.

result.result_summary: These were excluded; only the institutional and established-media results were retained.

why_it_matters: Automated monitoring of Hungarian procurement/fraud keywords will pull in junk domains; a domain allowlist is required.

description: The BHGY search entry point and the OLAF report index were referenced but their exact live paths were not confirmed by fetch in this pass; the redflags.eu project may be partially archived.

result.result_summary: Recorded as candidates with reduced confidence_score rather than omitted or asserted as verified.

why_it_matters: Downstream liveness verification should prioritise these three URLs; a non-200 here is a hypothesis (moved/archived), not proof of death.

description: Searched in both Hungarian and English for a tender aggregator or bid-monitoring service specialised in banking, payments, fintech or financial infrastructure procurement in Hungary. No such vertical specialist was found. The only sector segmentation observed anywhere was TendersOnTime's generic 'Hungary Banks Tenders' country+category page, which is an automated category slice of a global database rather than a domain-expert service.

result.result_summary: Zero Hungary-specific banking/payments tender specialists identified; all HU aggregators are horizontal/multi-sector.

why_it_matters: Means the run cannot outsource banking/payments filtering to a vendor. Sector filtering must be built in-house via CPV codes and buyer lists applied on top of horizontal aggregators, and recall will depend on our own keyword/CPV quality rather than a vendor's curation.

description: Several aggregators make strong coverage claims that could not be validated without paying: Tender-Értesítő's '1400+ monitored sources' and '78% more notifications than TED in 2024', TenderMonitor's 'EKR + Közbeszerzési Értesítő + TED + 100+ municipal sites', and Tendersinfo's '1.5M+ private tender results'. All are vendor marketing observed via search result summaries, not independently measured.

result.result_summary: Coverage claims recorded as vendor assertions only; no independent recall measurement performed.

why_it_matters: Procurement of a paid feed should not rest on marketing numbers. If any of these are adopted, a controlled recall test against a known set of HU banking/payments notices is needed before committing budget or treating the feed as authoritative.

description: kozbeszerzes.khf.hu, a distinctly branded and separately marketed Hungarian notice-monitoring service with its own subscription page, returned an HTTP 302 to https://www.tender-ertesito.hu/ when fetched. This is a single observation and is treated as a hypothesis of brand consolidation, not a confirmed merger or a dead site.

result.result_summary: khf.hu appears to redirect into Tender-Értesítő; independence unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: The Hungarian aggregator market may be more concentrated than the number of visible brands suggests. Counting khf.hu and Tender-Értesítő as two independent sources would overstate source redundancy and give false confidence in cross-validation.

description: Searched Hungarian-language terms for private-sector request-for-quote marketplaces where banks or financial institutions post non-public RFPs ('ajánlatkérés', 'magán beszerzés', 'beszerzési felhívás'). Only Tender-Értesítő and khf.hu claim private-procurement coverage as an add-on to public monitoring; no standalone Hungarian private RFP marketplace surfaced.

result.result_summary: No dedicated HU private-sector RFP marketplace found; private coverage exists only as a feature of public-notice aggregators.

why_it_matters: Commercial bank procurement in Hungary is largely invisible to any aggregator. Private-sector payments deals will need to be inferred from indirect signals (vendor press releases, supplier case studies, regulatory filings) rather than tender feeds.

description: For Mercell, Tenderio, EuroTenders and TenderAlerts.eu, targeted English searching did not surface explicit documentation of Hungarian national or below-threshold coverage. Mercell's material describes national/regional/EU consolidation generically; none confirmed EKR or Közbeszerzési Értesítő ingestion for Hungary.

result.result_summary: Pan-EU platforms confirmed to exist and to cover the EU broadly, but Hungary-specific depth is undocumented publicly.

why_it_matters: These platforms may add nothing beyond TED for Hungary, in which case paying for them duplicates a free official source. Depth must be tested before adoption, and TED-only coverage would miss exactly the below-threshold band this cell was created to capture.

description: TendersGo was described in detail in a third-party marketing article on gtbc.net (AI tender-document summarisation, unlimited Hungary email alerts) but its own canonical product domain did not appear in the search results obtained. It is recorded as a pointer, not as a verified aggregator.

result.result_summary: TendersGo product exists per third-party content; canonical domain not identified in this pass.

why_it_matters: Avoids inventing a plausible-looking URL. AI-summarisation of Hungarian-language tender documents would be genuinely useful given the language barrier, so the vendor is worth resolving in a later pass.

description: The cell brief lists 'Computerworld HU' as a target outlet. Media-industry reporting indicates Computerworld Hungary published its final issue on 20 December 2023 and was replaced by ComputerTrends (publisher Project029).

result.result_summary: computerworld.hu should not be treated as a live outlet; track computertrends.hu instead, plus the Computerworld archive for historical backfill.

why_it_matters: Prevents the pipeline from monitoring a dead domain and losing the CIO-level Hungarian IT trade coverage entirely.

description: Searched in Hungarian for trade-press coverage specifically of private-bank (non-public-sector) procurement of payment hardware/services — i.e. bank card-acceptance or terminal estate sourcing. No outlet was found that systematically reports such deals; coverage is sporadic and mostly vendor-press-release driven (FinTechZone, ProfitLine, Helló Sajtó).

result.result_summary: No specialised Hungarian journal covers private-bank payments sourcing as a beat.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed press would expose private-bank sourcing that has no published channel; in practice the press layer is thin and PR-mediated, so signals must be reconstructed from vendor announcements plus municipal/public tenders.

description: The Hungarian term 'portfólió' collides with the outlet name Portfolio.hu inside procurement notice titles (e.g. a tender for 'Portfólió és alrendszerek továbbfejlesztése'), polluting queries that combine 'Portfolio' with 'közbeszerzés'.

result.result_summary: Query 'Portfolio.hu bank informatikai szerződés tender nyert közbeszerzés' returned mostly procurement-notice aggregators rather than Portfolio articles.

why_it_matters: Query design must anchor on site: filters or the outlet's own search rather than free-text brand+topic combinations; flag 'portfólió' as a noisy term.

description: Napi.hu was included on the strength of the cell brief and general knowledge of the Hungarian business-press landscape; it did not surface directly in this run's result sets, so its current section structure, RSS availability and relevance density are unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: Listed as a candidate with lower confidence; requires a verification fetch.

why_it_matters: Avoids presenting an unconfirmed item as an evidenced discovery.

description: Searched in Hungarian for the sponsor/exhibitor roster of Portfolio Hitelezés 2026 and FinTechShow/BankTechShow 2025. Sponsorship pages exist and name a sponsorship contact and tier labels (Főszponzor, Arany/Ezüst/Bronz fokozat, Kiemelt támogató, Megoldáspartner), but no company-level sponsor list was retrievable from search snippets or a text fetch of the FinTechZone speakers page.

result.result_summary: Tier taxonomy captured; company names not captured. Likely client-side rendered or on a separate /tamogatok tab not yet fetched. This is a rendering/depth limitation, not evidence the lists do not exist.

why_it_matters: Company-level sponsor tiers are the highest-value signal in this cell; collection must use a headless renderer and must enumerate the per-event sponsor tab, not the overview page.

description: Searched in Hungarian for a standalone Hungarian payments-industry association (analogous to a national payments council or card-issuers' association) using terms such as 'fizetési szolgáltatók szövetsége', 'kártyakibocsátók', alongside Bankszövetség and Fintech Szövetség queries.

result.result_summary: No independent Hungarian payments-only trade association surfaced. Payments interests appear to be handled inside Magyar Bankszövetség working groups and via MAFISZ/HFA, with commercial conference organisers (IIR, Portfolio, FinTechZone) filling the convening role.

why_it_matters: Means the payments supplier map must be assembled from conference sponsor lists and bank-association working groups rather than from a single membership register.

description: The Magyar Fintech Szövetség (HFA) membership page was identified but its actual member roster did not appear in search results; only the existence of the page and general mission statements were retrievable.

result.result_summary: Page URL captured (hunfintech.com/membership/); roster content unconfirmed and must be fetched directly.

why_it_matters: The HFA roster is a core deliverable of this cell; it should be prioritised for a direct rendered fetch in the collection pass.

description: No Hungarian-language equivalent was found for a 'savings cooperative association' membership register — the Takarékszövetkezetek sector has been consolidated into MBH Bank, so the historic OTSZ/Takarékbank-era association terms returned no live membership directory.

result.result_summary: Sector consolidation appears to have removed a formerly distinct association layer; no live roster found.

why_it_matters: Analysts should not expect a separate cooperative-bank supplier channel in Hungary; that demand now sits inside MBH Bank's procurement.

description: Searches for chamber and association member directories repeatedly returned commercial B2B data brokers (Apollo.io, Lusha, uzleti.hu) rather than the primary directories.

result.result_summary: These are lead-generation resellers of contact data, not authoritative membership registers.

why_it_matters: They should be excluded from the source set: low credibility, unclear provenance, and personal-data/legal exposure under GDPR.

description: No Hungarian-language aggregator or feed exists that specifically indexes bank/payments IT job postings by named platform (core banking, card management, ISO 20022). Signals must be reconstructed from general job boards with keyword filters.

result.result_summary: Queries on Hungarian platform terms returned mostly foreign (Singapore, US, Vietnam) T24/Temenos roles plus generic Hungarian bank listings; no HU-specific niche board surfaced.

why_it_matters: Collection for this cell cannot be a single feed; it needs a maintained keyword+employer watchlist across several boards, raising cost and false-negative risk.

description: Hungarian job ads largely use untranslated English platform names ('core banking', 'Temenos', 'T24', 'API', 'PSD2') embedded in Hungarian sentences; there is no stable Hungarian equivalent for most platform terms.

result.result_summary: Observed hybrid usage such as 'Core rendszerszervező' at MKB and 'core banking' inside otherwise Hungarian ad text.

why_it_matters: Local-language-only queries will systematically miss postings; every keyword list must pair the Hungarian role/verb terms ('bevezetés', 'migráció', 'szakértő', 'projektmenedzser') with English platform nouns.

description: Site-scoped queries against Hungarian IT trade press (bitport.hu, hwsw.hu, itbusiness.hu) returned no article hits for bank IT contracts or the MBH integration.

result.result_summary: The query returned only an archived 2021 IT Business PDF and unrelated pages; no live article-level results.

why_it_matters: These outlets very likely do carry relevant coverage; the gap is a discovery-tooling limitation, not evidence of absence. On-site search or sitemap crawling is required rather than general web search.

description: No Hungarian-language 'supplier call' / subcontracting portal specific to ATM, POS or payment-terminal supply chains was found.

result.result_summary: Hungarian subcontracting queries surfaced only generic public-procurement notices and SME grant programmes, not bank/acquirer supplier calls.

why_it_matters: Second-tier supplier demand in the payments hardware chain is likely transacted privately (direct RFQ), so subcontracting signals must be inferred from award-notice subcontractor fields and vendor hiring instead.

description: The two richest indirect sources for this cell - LinkedIn and Indeed/Glassdoor - are login-walled and/or ToS-restricted against automation.

result.result_summary: LinkedIn company/profile URLs were visible in search results only; no anonymous full-content access obtained.

why_it_matters: The highest-yield signal (vendor Budapest delivery-team ramp-ups, programme names in employee titles) cannot be automated and needs a budgeted manual analyst routine.

description: Annual-report capex/IT-vendor disclosure was located as PDFs but the specific IT-investment and supplier lines were not read in this run.

result.result_summary: OTP's 2025 integrated annual report and Q4 results PDFs were identified on bet.hu but not parsed.

why_it_matters: Whether Hungarian bank reports actually name IT vendors (vs. only aggregate intangible capex) determines how much weight this signal class can carry; must be tested on one report before scaling.

description: No public tender/notice board was found for UniCredit group procurement. Searches in Italian ('fornitori', 'portale acquisti', 'appalti') surfaced only supply-chain-finance products, a login-only group corporate portal, and union reporting — no supplier opportunity listing.

result.result_summary: UniCredit group sourcing appears to be conducted entirely on closed platforms (reportedly SAP Ariba), with no public award notices for Hungarian subsidiary spend.

why_it_matters: Contract intelligence for UniCredit Bank Hungary cannot be collected from a primary procurement feed; it must be inferred from union reporting, vendor case studies, MNB outsourcing disclosures and press.

description: No dedicated KBC Group supplier/procurement portal or sustainable-procurement policy page was located via Dutch/English search; results returned unrelated companies (KBR) and K&H product pages.

result.result_summary: KBC's supplier-facing procurement channel was not identified in this pass.

why_it_matters: K&H Bank is one of the largest Hungarian banks; without locating KBC group procurement, the Belgian leg of this cell has only indirect coverage.

description: Targeted searches for publicly announced CEE regional framework agreements naming Hungary as an included market (banking/payments vendor rollouts) returned no such announcement.

result.result_summary: No press release or award notice for a CEE-wide framework deal with explicit Hungarian scope was found.

why_it_matters: Confirms that regional framework awards are largely undisclosed and must be reconstructed from vendor case studies, group annual reports and subsidiary outsourcing registers rather than notices.

description: No Hungary-scoped EBRD or EIB financial-sector procurement notice was individually confirmed in this pass; only the platforms, filters and one EBRD credit-line context (Erste Bank Hungary, Raiffeisen Bank Hungary as partner FIs) were established.

result.result_summary: Platform-level coverage confirmed; item-level Hungarian notices not yet enumerated.

why_it_matters: Volume and cadence of Hungary-relevant IFI notices is still unknown, so collection frequency cannot yet be sized.

description: Hungarian-language searching produced strong results for 'beszerzés', 'beszállító', 'kiszervezés' and 'csoportszintű', but there is no established Hungarian term or public register specifically denoting 'parent-group framework agreement awarded abroad covering the Hungarian subsidiary'.

result.result_summary: The concept central to this cell has no native Hungarian search handle.

why_it_matters: Hungarian-language monitoring will systematically under-detect cross-border framework awards; detection must run in German, Italian, Dutch and English against the parent groups.

description: Searches in Hungarian and English for a GIRO Zrt. procurement/supplier page (giro.hu közbeszerzés, ajánlati felhívás, beszerzés, szállító) returned no dedicated tender or supplier-registration section on giro.hu. GIRO's largest known supplier selection (Nets A/S for the instant payment system, 2019) was reported by trade press, not by a public GIRO notice page we could locate.

result.result_summary: No giro.hu procurement page identified; GIRO's status as a registered ajánlatkérő remains unconfirmed and must be checked in the EKR ajánlatkérő nyilvántartás.

why_it_matters: GIRO is the operator of BKR and AFR — the single most relevant payments buyer in this cell. If it does not publish tenders on its own site, the only routes are EKR/KBA filings (if it is an ajánlatkérő) and trade-press/vendor announcements, which changes the collection design substantially.

description: For KELER Zrt. and KELER KSZF Zrt. only generic 'Közérdekű adatok' landing pages were found; no procurement-specific subpage (közbeszerzési terv, hirdetmények) was identified in this pass, in either hu or en searches.

result.result_summary: Buyer-side visibility for the CSD/CCP is limited to the general public-data page; the procurement branch, if any, is unlocated.

why_it_matters: Post-trade infrastructure procurement (settlement, collateral, connectivity) would otherwise be a strong signal; if KELER discloses nothing procurement-specific, EKR/KBA lookups become the only route.

description: Search snippets indicated that Magyar Posta's beszerzesek_palyazatok page currently shows no active procurement announcements and invites visitors to return later.

result.result_summary: The Posta tender listing appears to be episodic/empty between procedures — an empty fetch must not be read as a dead source.

why_it_matters: A collector that treats an empty listing as failure would drop one of the highest-value buyers in this cell; the page must be polled continuously and the archived static PDF notices used for backfill.

description: The Magyar Államkincstár procurement/közérdekű adatok subpage was not pinned down to an exact URL; only the activity-description and payment-notices pages were confirmed by search results. Recorded as unverified rather than absent.

result.result_summary: Treasury procurement disclosure branch exists by legal obligation but its precise location on allamkincstar.gov.hu is unresolved.

why_it_matters: The Treasury is arguably the largest state payments buyer in scope; leaving its disclosure page unmapped is a material hole in the cell.

description: Magyar Posta routes tender documentation and bid submission through SAP Ariba Sourcing, requiring supplier registration; the substantive documents are therefore not openly collectable.

result.result_summary: Only the fronting public hirdetmény PDF is openly available; detail sits behind authentication.

why_it_matters: Caps the depth of intelligence obtainable on Posta procurements without a registered supplier identity — a decision the user must make deliberately, not something to automate.

description: This pass did not surface procurement pages for adjacent state-influenced financial bodies beyond the named eight (e.g. OBA/National Deposit Insurance Fund, Szanálási Alap, Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület, Nemzeti Adó- és Vámhivatal payment functions). No hu-language queries were run for them within this cell's budget.

result.result_summary: Actor map is complete for the assigned eight but not extended to plausible neighbours.

why_it_matters: Adjacent state buyers procure comparable payments/cash infrastructure and could be missed entirely by a buyer-name-filtered feed.

description: No national aggregator of Hungarian municipal council agendas/minutes (képviselő-testületi előterjesztések, jegyzőkönyvek) was found. or.njt.hu aggregates only local DECREES (önkormányzati rendeletek), not agendas or minutes, and several municipalities state that minutes are inspectable at the mayor's office during office hours.

result.result_summary: Searched in Hungarian for council minutes on bank selection; results were individual municipal sites plus the decree register, no cross-municipality index.

why_it_matters: The earliest and often the only signal for sub-threshold municipal account/POS deals lives in these documents; without a central index, collection must be per-buyer and will be expensive and incomplete.

description: No specific POS-terminal or card-acquiring procurement notice by a Hungarian hospital or university was located within this run; Semmelweis procurement documents surfaced were for unrelated categories (e.g. SPECT equipment).

result.result_summary: Hungarian query combining kórház/egyetem + POS terminál + közbeszerzés returned buyer procurement portals and bank acquiring product pages, not notices.

why_it_matters: Cannot yet confirm whether health/education card acceptance is tendered at all or absorbed via EFER/central framework contracts; this shapes whether the cell has a real notice stream.

description: redflags.eu is reported as not updated since 27 October 2023 owing to TED data-provision changes.

result.result_summary: Search result text explicitly states the halt; treated as historic-only, not dead.

why_it_matters: Prevents using it for live risk scoring of current municipal banking tenders; a replacement risk-indicator layer must be built in-house from TED/EKR data.

description: EKR document access and bidding require personal + organisational registration; only the eljárástár browse layer appears open. Not verified in this run whether the browse layer is machine-readable or rate-limited.

result.result_summary: Documentation and guides consistently describe mandatory registration for use; public search described as available since June 2024.

why_it_matters: Determines whether EKR can be automated or must be supplemented by the gazette and commercial aggregators.

description: No dedicated procurement/disclosure page for Volánbusz Zrt. was confirmed in this run (searches returned BKV and Fővárosi Vízművek instead, plus an archived KMKK page).

result.result_summary: Hungarian query on Kbt. 43. § disclosures returned no Volánbusz page.

why_it_matters: Volánbusz is a nationwide bus operator and a major ticketing-payments buyer; its notices may only be reachable via EKR/CoRe buyer search.

description: K&H Bank (KBC group) — repeated Hungarian-language searches on kh.hu for beszállítói regisztráció, szállítóinknak, beszerzési alapelvek and beszállítói etikai kódex returned only retail/insurance customer portals and the career portal.

result.result_summary: No vendor registration page, no RFP page, no procurement contact found on kh.hu. Only the K&H Csoport fenntarthatósági irányelvek document describes supplier CSR contractual requirements.

why_it_matters: K&H is a top-3 Hungarian bank; its IT/facilities spend is entirely invisible externally. Access must be pursued via KBC group procurement or relationship channels, not open sources.

description: MBH Bank — no szállítói/beszállítói portál, no vendor registration and no RFP page located; searches surfaced only the MBH Beszállítói Faktoring (supply-chain finance) product and the merchant (kereskedői) POS portal.

result.result_summary: Only public sourcing evidence is the procurement/bidding chapter of the MBH Etikai Kódex.

why_it_matters: MBH is Hungary's second-largest bank and a large post-merger consolidation buyer; the absence of any public channel means its sourcing is trackable only via ethics-code language, MNB outsourcing regime, press and direct contact.

description: GRÁNIT Bank — Hungarian searches on beszerzés, beszállító, pályázat and ajánlatkérés returned no procurement or supplier page at all; the only procurement-adjacent hit was Gránit's participation, alongside MBH and OTP, as a bidder in the MFB Pont Plusz public procurement.

result.result_summary: Zero vendor-facing content located for Gránit Bank.

why_it_matters: Gránit is the fastest-growing digital bank in the cell and a likely buyer of payments/IT services, but is entirely opaque from open sources; monitoring must rely on press, EKR bidder records and vendor-side announcements.

description: The Hungarian term 'beszállítói' is heavily overloaded: at MBH, UniCredit and others 'beszállítói finanszírozás / beszállítói faktoring / beszállítói program' means reverse-factoring supply-chain finance SOLD to clients, not the bank's own purchasing.

result.result_summary: The majority of bank-site hits for 'beszállítói' were supply-chain-finance products, not procurement.

why_it_matters: Any automated Hungarian collection on 'beszállítói' will be dominated by false positives; queries must pair it with beszerzés / szállítói regisztráció / pályáztatás / ajánlatkérés and exclude faktoring / finanszírozás.

description: None of the nine private banks in this cell publishes open tender notices (versenyfelhívás / ajánlati felhívás) the way Magyar Telekom does. OTP explicitly routes RFx through invitation-only SAP Ariba events; Erste routes them through the Erste Group Procurements online platform.

result.result_summary: No open RFP/RFI listings found for any private Hungarian bank.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: for these banks, only onboarding/policy pages and platform identification are collectable; award-level intelligence must come from indirect sources (vendor press releases, registry, MNB outsourcing, MFB benchmarks).

description: The MNB outsourcing (kiszervezés) register — the richest structured bank-to-vendor contract dataset in Hungary — is a supervisory filing, not a public register.

result.result_summary: The 58/2015 MNB rendelet and 7/2020 ajánlás describe mandatory notification and register content, but the data itself sits with the supervisor via the ERA portal.

why_it_matters: Sets a hard ceiling on open-source vendor-contract visibility; only the rules, not the records, are collectable. Any future DORA register-of-information disclosure would be a step change and should be watched.

description: erstegroupprocurement.com and epp.unicreditbank.hu/partnerkapu were identified by reference/search but not fetched in this pass.

result.result_summary: URLs recorded with reduced confidence; scope and liveness unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: Both are plausible direct vendor entry points; a single failed or skipped fetch is not evidence they are dead or irrelevant and they should be checked in the deterministic verification pass.

description: No dedicated, structured registry of vendor-announced private-sector contract wins in Hungary exists; there is no Hungarian equivalent of a commercial 'deal tracker' covering bank/retail technology awards.

result.result_summary: Searches in both hu and en returned only scattered vendor newsrooms and trade-press articles; no aggregator scoped to Hungary.

why_it_matters: Collection must be vendor-by-vendor (many small crawls) rather than one high-yield feed, raising ongoing cost and increasing miss risk.

description: Hungarian-language queries built on 'sajtóközlemény' + 'szállító' + 'bank' surfaced mostly banking-association and central-bank press pages, not vendor win announcements.

result.result_summary: Top HU results were bankszovetseg.hu and mnb.hu press rooms plus academic history material — off-cell for vendor announcements.

why_it_matters: Hungarian vendors appear to publish wins under 'referencia'/'esettanulmány'/'ügyfeleink' rather than 'sajtóközlemény'; query vocabulary must be adjusted to those terms.

description: No Hungary-specific card-issuing/processing vendor win announcement was located for 2025-2026 despite targeted search (issuer-processor space).

result.result_summary: Searches returned generic issuer-processor marketing pages and non-Hungarian partnerships only.

why_it_matters: Card issuing/processing is a core Printec-adjacent segment; absence of evidence here is a discovery gap, not evidence of no deals.

description: Vendor newsroom URLs for NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Intellect Design, GK Software and Barion were inferred from the vendor's known site structure rather than opened during this pass.

result.result_summary: Not fetched in this run; liveness unknown.

why_it_matters: These need the deterministic verification pass; do not treat the URL paths as confirmed.

description: No public, structured 'reference list' of banking-sector engagements was found for the Hungarian arms of NTT Data, DXC Technology or Accenture. English and Hungarian searches surfaced no HU-specific banking case studies for NTT Data HU or DXC HU.

result.result_summary: Global case-study libraries exist but were not confirmed to contain HU banking references in this pass; HU-entity reference pages were not located.

why_it_matters: These are significant employers in HU financial-services delivery, so their engagements will have to be inferred indirectly (e-beszámoló financials, bank outsourcing registers, job ads, LinkedIn) rather than read off a reference page.

description: No consolidated public register was found that lists private-sector (bank-to-integrator) contract awards in Hungary. Public procurement data covers only public buyers; private bank IT deals appear only via vendor PR, bank outsourcing annexes, or trade press.

result.result_summary: Searches for HU bank IT contract registers returned only public-procurement portals and vendor marketing.

why_it_matters: Roughly half the cell's target universe (commercial bank spend) has no authoritative source; coverage must be assembled from the outsourcing-register and vendor-PR routes, which are incomplete and lagging.

description: Several key Hungarian terms are noisy: 'referencia' also means credit reference/testimonial; 'keretszerződés' vs 'keretmegállapodás' are legally distinct but used loosely; 'pénzforgalom' spans payments traffic and accounting; '4iG' matches unrelated ticker/market chatter.

result.result_summary: Query results mixed stock-market commentary with contract news for 4iG; consultancy searches returned thought-leadership rather than engagements.

why_it_matters: Naive keyword collection will produce a high false-positive rate; queries need to be co-constrained with buyer names, CPV codes or document types.

description: For CEE-regional integrators headquartered outside Hungary (Asseco PL, Comarch PL, Sygnity, Ness), no Hungarian-language corpus of banking references was found; their HU-relevant disclosures appear only in Polish or English.

result.result_summary: Hungarian-language searches returned no HU-market case studies for these vendors.

why_it_matters: Cross-border integrator activity into Hungary may be systematically under-detected by a HU-language-only collection strategy; Polish and English collection is required for these actors.

description: OpenTender data is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial), and Nemzeti Cégtár/OPTEN detail data is a paid commercial product with scraping restrictions.

result.result_summary: Licence terms observed on the source pages themselves.

why_it_matters: The cheapest analytical shortcuts carry licence risk for a commercial intelligence product; primary EKR/TED/Közbeszerzési Értesítő collection should be the backbone, with aggregators used for validation only.

description: No public, Hungary-specific list of Visa/Mastercard licensed acquirers or scheme-certified terminal vendors was found. Scheme licensing/certification lists appear to be issued to members, not published per country.

result.result_summary: EN searches returned only generic scheme PayFac/acquirer model documents and third-party explainers; no HU acquirer roster.

why_it_matters: The acquirer/certification universe for HU must be reconstructed indirectly from MNB registers, acquirer ÁSZF documents and trade press rather than from a scheme list.

description: No official public directory of qvik-accepting merchants or of all qvik technical/sub-aggregator providers was located; reporting indicates only a small set of sub-aggregators (OTP Mobil, Raiffeisen mentioned in trade press) but no maintained scheme list surfaced.

result.result_summary: HU searches on qvik szolgáltató lista / elfogadóhelyek returned bank product pages and media, not a registry.

why_it_matters: qvik ecosystem participant tracking will need press + provider-site monitoring, with MNB/GIRO pages checked for an eventual official participant list.

description: General web search does not index EKR procedure content or Közbeszerzési Értesítő notice bodies well; payments-specific HU tenders could not be enumerated from search engines alone.

result.result_summary: Queries returned portal landing pages plus one incidental VPOS tender PDF hosted by the contracting authority.

why_it_matters: A2 payments tender coverage must run against EKR/KÉ/TED search interfaces and APIs directly; search-engine-based discovery will systematically under-report.

description: Private-sector merchant acquiring RFPs (retail chains, telcos, e-commerce) are not published anywhere public; only the outcome surfaces, usually as a vendor press release.

result.result_summary: No HU or EN query produced a public private-sector acquiring RFP.

why_it_matters: Most acquiring volume changes hands outside public procurement, so award-notice monitoring alone will miss the majority of the market.

description: No public, documented API was found for the official Hungarian registers in this cell — neither e-cegjegyzek.hu, e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu, cegkozlony.hu nor MNB Intézménykereső surfaced API documentation in hu or en searches.

result.result_summary: All appear to be HTML search interfaces only; bulk access to beszámoló data is offered as a paid dataset sale ('beszámoló állomány értékesítése') and grouped queries require an emailed request form.

why_it_matters: Collection design must assume polite HTML scraping or a commercial licence rather than an API, which affects cost, latency and legal posture.

description: OPTEN's public pages describe company-information services and monitoring but no API endpoint/documentation was located; whether a machine-readable feed exists is unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: Searched 'Opten Nemzeti Cégtár céginformáció adatbázis API' in hu; results returned service and manual pages, no API spec.

why_it_matters: Prevents scoping an automated commercial feed without a direct vendor enquiry.

description: No Hungary-specific Bisnode/Dun & Bradstreet register or product page was surfaced in this run; the seed's 'Bisnode' reference could not be resolved to a live HU source.

result.result_summary: Bisnode did not appear in any of the hu or en result sets executed for this cell.

why_it_matters: Bisnode has been absorbed into Dun & Bradstreet in several markets; the HU entity/product name likely changed and needs a dedicated follow-up search.

description: NAV does not publish a 'contracted partner database' of the kind implied by the seed query; NAV's public databases cover taxpayer status (áfaalany, KOMA, enforcement) rather than contract counterparties.

result.result_summary: hu search for NAV céginformáció / szerződéses partner adatbázis returned only taxpayer-status query tools and NAV's own üvegzseb disclosure lists.

why_it_matters: Contract-level evidence for public bodies must come from üvegzseb/kozadat.hu and the procurement portals (other cells), not from NAV.

description: Hungarian case law and practice hold that the Banking Act (Hpt.) is lex specialis to the Info Act, and courts have accepted that the entire contract concluded with a financial institution can fall under bank secrecy (banktitok), so contract data that would otherwise be publishable under the 5 M Ft rule can be withheld precisely when the counterparty is a bank.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'megtagadható-e a banktitoknak minősülő közérdekű adat kiadása' returned legal commentary describing successful refusals on bank-secrecy grounds.

why_it_matters: This is the single biggest systematic blind spot for this cell: banking and payment contracts are exactly the category most likely to be redacted or withheld in the contract-transparency archives, so absence in kozadat.hu or a body's III.4 list must never be read as absence of a deal.

description: As of August 2026 the Magyar Nemzeti Bank is refusing to release its contracts above HUF 5 million concluded since January 2025, arguing it is not a budgetary body; Transparency International Hungary has complained to NAIH and the case is under investigation.

result.result_summary: Multiple independent Hungarian outlets (Portfolio, 444, Economx, Contextus) report the refusal and the NAIH complaint.

why_it_matters: The central bank — a major buyer of payment infrastructure and financial IT — is currently a hole in the contract-transparency record. The NAIH decision, when it lands, will determine whether a large body of MNB contract data becomes collectable, and should be tracked as a scheduled event.

description: No documented public bulk-download or open API was confirmed for EKR, the Közbeszerzési Hatóság databases (KBA/CoRe), or kozadat.hu during this pass — only human-facing search interfaces and, for EKR, an email notification service.

result.result_summary: Local-language query 'EKR nyílt adat letöltés' returned portal and training material but no open-data/API documentation.

why_it_matters: Collection design for the national layer will likely depend on scraping or on the EU TED/Opentender mirrors, which have different coverage (TED only above EU thresholds) and different lag. Worth a dedicated verification pass and, if needed, a FOI request via KiMitTud for machine-readable exports.

description: K-Monitor has publicly criticised the new state public-spending database as poor ('lesújtó'), per Szabad Európa reporting on the K-Monitor blog.

result.result_summary: Found via local-language search; the specific critique post on k.blog.hu was not read in this pass.

why_it_matters: Suggests the statutory central register (kozadat.hu / KIK) may be incomplete or badly structured; NGO archives should be treated as complements, not fallbacks, and the critique should be read before setting confidence on registry-derived counts.

description: An automated fetch of https://k-monitor.hu/adatbazisok returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.

result.result_summary: Single failed fetch; other k-monitor.hu and adatbazis.k-monitor.hu URLs appeared normally in search results.

why_it_matters: Almost certainly bot defence rather than a dead page — recorded as a hypothesis, not a verdict. Collection should use a browser-like client for this domain.

description: The aHáló network database was described on K-Monitor's activities page as 'ahalo.hu', but that hostname was not independently confirmed reachable in this pass, and the seeded alternative 'halo.k-monitor.hu' produced no direct hit.

result.result_summary: Only the K-Monitor descriptive page was confirmed as a search hit.

why_it_matters: The candidate is recorded with a reduced confidence score; the deterministic liveness pass should resolve the correct hostname before collection is scheduled.
